rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kawthar is the most abundant and beneficial river in Paradise; it flows swiftly like an arrow.
rows.anchor: لأنه أكثر أنهار الجنة خيرا، وذلك النهر عجاج يطرد مثل السهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its clay is fragrant musk, and its pebbles are ruby, emerald, and pearl.
rows.anchor: طينه المسك الآذفر، ورضراضه الياقوت، والزبرجد، واللؤلؤ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The river is whiter than snow, softer than foam, and sweeter than honey.
rows.anchor: أشد بياضا من الثلج وألين من الزبد، وأحلى من العسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its banks have hollow pearl domes, each one a parasang long and wide.
rows.anchor: حافتاه قباب الدر المجوف، كل قبة طولها فرسخ في فرسخ، وعرضها فرسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each dome has four thousand golden doors and a wife from the houris with seventy servants.
rows.anchor: عليها أربعة آلاف مصراع من ذهب، في كل قبة زوجة من الحور العين، لها سبعون خادما

rows.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
rows.claim: Gabriel tells the Prophet that the domes are the dwellings of his wives in Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال جبريل، عليه السلام: هذه مساكن أزواجك في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four rivers flow from al-Kawthar for Paradise's people: water, wine, milk, and honey, as described in Surat Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يتفجر من الكوثر أربعة أنهار لأهل الجنان التى ذكر الله عز وجل في سورة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم: الماء، والحمر، واللبن، والعسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Pray to your Lord” means the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: { فصل لربك } يعني الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sacrifice” means slaughtering sacrificial camels on the Day of Sacrifice; idolaters neither pray nor slaughter for God.
rows.anchor: البدن يوم النحر، فإن المشركين لا يصلون ولا يذبحون لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-As ibn Wa'il called the Prophet “the one cut off” after the Prophet's son Abdullah died; men without a surviving son were called abtar.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد توفى ابنه عبدالله، وكان الرجل إذا مات ولم يكن له من بعده ابن يرثه، سمى الأبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means the Prophet's hater—identified as al-As ibn Wa'il—is cut off from goodness, while Muhammad will be remembered throughout Muslim worship and public life.
rows.anchor: يعني أن مبغضك هو الأبتر، يعني العاص بن وائل السهمي، هو الذي أبتر من الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah was revealed about Quraysh mockers after Satan, during the Prophet's recitation of al-Najm, put the “high cranes” words on his tongue while he was drowsy.
rows.anchor: نزلتفي المستهزئين من قريش، وذلك أن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ بمكة

rows.speaker: المستهزئون من قريش
rows.claim: The mockers offered a religious compromise: each side would worship the other's deity and enter part of the other's religion, or they would mutually renounce each other's gods.
rows.anchor: ندخل معكفي بعض دينك ونعبد إلهك، وتدخل معنافي بعض ديننا وتعبد آلهتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl, Shayba and Utba ibn Rabi'a, Umayya ibn Khalaf, al-As ibn Wa'il, and Quraysh's mockers made the proposal at the Kaaba's rear in the evening.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو جهل بن هشام، وشيبة وعتبة ابنا ربيعة، وأمية بن خلف، والعاص بن وائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's refusal means he does not worship their idols, which they worship at that time.
rows.anchor: لا أعبد آلهتكم التي تعبدون اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means that, at that time, the addressees do not worship the Prophet's God.
rows.anchor: إلهي الذي أعبده اليوم { مآ أعبد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet will not worship what they worship after that day.
rows.anchor: ولا أنآ عابد ما عبدتم } [آية: 4] فيما بعد اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will not worship what the Prophet worships after that day.
rows.anchor: ولا أنتم عابدون مآ أعبد } [آية: 5] فيما بعد اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final verse means they keep the religion they follow, while the Prophet follows his own.
rows.anchor: لكم دينكم } الذي أنتم عليه { ولي دين } [آية: 6] الذي أنا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Prophet departed, some said he had disavowed them; they insulted and harmed him.
rows.anchor: ثم انصرف عنهم، فقال بعضهم: تبرأها منكم فشتموه وآذوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil says the surah was abrogated by the sword verse ordering the killing of polytheists wherever found.
rows.anchor: ثم نسختها آية السيففي براءة: فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah was revealed after the conquests of Mecca and al-Taif.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه السورة بعد فتح مكة والطائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those entering God's religion in groups are the people of Yemen.
rows.anchor: ورأيت الناس يدخلون في دين الله } يعني أهل اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In crowds” means whole tribes and peoples arriving together from every direction, rather than just one, two, or three people.
rows.anchor: من كل وجه زمرا، القبيلة بأسرها والقوم بأجمعهم، ليس بواحد ولا اثنين ولا ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mass conversions signal that the Prophet's appointed end has come near.
rows.anchor: ليس بواحد ولا اثنين ولا ثلاثة، فقد حضر أجلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Glorify with praise” means to increase remembrance of the Lord.
rows.anchor: فسبح بحمد ربك } يقول: فأكثر ذكر ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek forgiveness is for sins, and God accepts repentance from those seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: يقول: فأكثر ذكر ربك { واستغفره } من الذنوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah was a sign of the Prophet's death: he recited it to Abu Bakr and Umar, who rejoiced, while Ibn Abbas wept; the Prophet affirmed Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: كانت هذه السورة آية موت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأها على أبى بكر وعمر ففرحا، وسمعها عبد الله بن عباس فبكى

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet lived eighty days after reciting the surah, then rubbed Ibn Abbas's head and prayed that God grant him religious understanding and teach him interpretation.
rows.anchor: فعاش النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعدها ثمانين يوما،ومسح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده على رأس ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab was the Prophet's uncle, named Abd al-Uzza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: واسمه عبدالعزى بن عبدالمطلب، وهو عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was called Abu Lahab because his cheeks were red as if fire burned from them.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي أبو لهب لأن وجنتيه كانتا حمراوين، كأنما يلتهب منهما النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After 26:214 commanded warning near relatives, the Prophet asked Ali to prepare food and invite Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: يعني بني هاشم، وبني المطلب، وهما ابنا عبد مناف بن قصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali prepared one sheep and a bowl of milk for thirty-nine men; they all ate and drank their fill.
rows.anchor: وهم أربعون رجلا غير رجل، على رجل شاة، وعس من لبن، فأكلوا حتى شبعوا

rows.speaker: أبو لهب
rows.claim: Abu Lahab accused Muhammad of sorcery, saying ten of their men normally eat a whole sheep and drink a bowl of milk, yet Muhammad fed forty with a sheep and milk.
rows.anchor: لهذا ما سحركم به، الرجال العشرة منا يأكلون الجذعة، ويشربون العس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was distressed and did not warn them that night, so he asked Ali to prepare a second meal; after they ate, he announced he was God's warner and bearer of good news and urged them to believe and obey.
rows.anchor: فلما سمع ذلك منه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شق عليه، ولم ينذرهم تلك الليلة

rows.speaker: أبو لهب
rows.claim: Abu Lahab cursed Muhammad for summoning them and then the surah was revealed about him.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو لهب: تبا لك، يا محمد، سائر اليوم لهذا دعوتنا؟ فأنزل الله عز وجل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Perished Abu Lahab's hands, and he perished” means that Abu Lahab lost.
rows.anchor: يعني وخسر أبو لهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wealth cannot help him in the afterlife; what he earned means his sons Utba, Utayba, and Mutabb, since children are a man's earnings.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة { وما كسب } [آية: 2] يعني أولاده عتبة وعتيبة ومتعب لأن ولده من كسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab will enter a flaming fire that has no smoke.
rows.anchor: يعني سيغشى أبو لهب { نارا ذات لهب } [آية: 3] ليس لها دخان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wife was Umm Jamil bint Harb, sister of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
rows.anchor: وهى أم جميل بنت حرب، وهى أخت أبي سفيان بن حرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Carrier of firewood” means she placed all kinds of piercing thorn on the Prophet's path to wound him.
rows.anchor: يعني كل شوك يعقر كانت تلقيه على طريق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليعقره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rope around Umm Jamil's neck on Judgment Day is an iron chain.
rows.anchor: في عنقها يوم القيامة { حبل من مسد } [آية: 5] يعني سلسلة من حديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angered by the surah, Umm Jamil took sheep dung, blood, and filth to throw on and disgrace the Prophet; Abu Bakr warned him as she approached.
rows.anchor: أن تحمل ما يكون في بطن الشاة من الفرث والدم والقذر، فانطلقت لتستدل على النبي

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Abu Bakr to let Umm Jamil enter because she would not see him.
rows.anchor: ثم قال لأبى بكر، رحمة الله عليه: " دعها تدخل، فإنها لن ترانى "

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed that God take her sight.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " اللهم خذ ببصرها " ، أو كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm Jamil saw Abu Bakr but did not see the Prophet, although they were in the same place.
rows.anchor: فدخلت أم جميل البيت، فرأت أبا بكر، رحمة الله عليه، ولم تر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكانا جميعا في مكان واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm Jamil said she came because she heard the Prophet had insulted her family; Abu Bakr denied it, she accepted his word, praised him as truthful, and said people had lied about Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قالت: أحق ما تقول يا أبا بكر، قال: نعم، فقالت: أما إنك لصادق، وأنت الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Utba ibn Abu Lahab announced to Quraysh that he disbelieved in al-Najm, the first surah the Prophet had openly recited; the Prophet prayed for a predatory animal to kill him, and Utba became so afraid that he scarcely stopped at night.
rows.anchor: إذا رجعتم إلى مكة، فاخبروا محمدا بأني كفرت ب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While travelling to Syria, Utba refused to stop at night from fear; his companions forced him to camp before dawn, where he surrounded himself and his camels with guards and baggage.
rows.anchor: فهجر بالليل، فسار يومه وليلته،وهم أن لا ينزل حتى يصبح، فلما كان قبيل الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lion led by an angel entered the guarded camp and ate Utba while he lay among his men and camels; they found only his bones and did not know what had happened.
rows.anchor: فجاء الأسد، ومعه ملك يقوده، فألقى الله عز وجل على الإبل السكينة، فسكنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the “cursed be man” passage as about Utba, after he said he disbelieved in the Quran revealed with al-Najm.
rows.anchor: قتل الإنسان يعني لعن الإنسان مآ أكفره [عبس: 17] يعني عتبة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih reports through Abdullah ibn Thabit and his father that Quraysh and Umm Jamil said they disobeyed and rejected the Prophet they called Mudhammam.
rows.anchor: حدثنا عبدالله بن ثابت، قال: حدثنا أبي، قال: حدثنا أبو صالح، قال: كانت قريش وأم جميل تقول

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said God's kindness was that Quraysh disparaged Mudhammam while he himself was Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ومن لطف الله أن قريشا تذم مذمما، وأنا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “One” and “the Self-Sufficient Master” mean God is one with no partner.
rows.anchor: تعنى أحد لا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amir ibn al-Tufayl claimed many would follow him if he accepted Islam and stay away if he refused, then demanded that the Prophet grant him control over the nomads and settled people.
rows.anchor: أما والله لئن دخلت في دينك ليدخلن من خلفى، ولئن امتنعت ليمتنعن من خلفي

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet rejected Amir's demand for special territorial conditions, saying Islam permits no such conditions.
rows.anchor: قال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا شرط في الإسلام "

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet refused Amir's request to succeed him, saying there would be no prophet after him.
rows.anchor: قال: فاجعل لي الخلافة بعدك، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا نبى بعدي "

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet refused Amir's request to outrank the Companions, but said Amir could be their brother if he embraced Islam well.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا، ولكنك أخوهم، إن أحسنت إسلامك "

rows.speaker: عامر بن الطفيل
rows.claim: Amir asked to count Bilal, Khabbab, Salman, and Ja'al as his brothers; after the Prophet agreed, Amir threatened to raise a thousand chestnut horses with a thousand young men.
rows.anchor: فتجعلنى أخا بلال وخباب بن الأرت، وسلمان الفارسى، وجعال، قال: " نعم " ، فغضب

rows.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
rows.claim: Gabriel told the Prophet that God would send a thousand angels for each enemy, each with a neck a year's journey long and thick; one would suffice, but God wanted to show the number of His forces.
rows.anchor: لأثيرن على كل واحد منهم ألفا من الملائكة، طول عنق أحدهم مسيرة سنة، وغلظها مسيرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amir and his friend al-Arbad returned intending to kill the Prophet; an angel crushed al-Arbad's abdomen, while Amir asked about the identity and size of the Prophet's troops.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم علم ما يريدان، قال: وجاء ملك من الملائكة فعصر بطن الأربد بن قيس

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said his troops were more numerous than Amir had threatened.
rows.anchor: قال: " جنودى وهم أكثر مما ذكرت لك "

rows.speaker: عامر بن الطفيل
rows.claim: Amir asked the Prophet for God's name, nature, intimate friend, means, number, father, clan, and brother.
rows.anchor: فأخبرنى ما اسم ربك؟ وما هو؟ ومن خليله؟ وما حيلته؟ وكم هو؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs of the pre-Islamic period used to take intimate friends; the surah answers questions about God's name, number, food, lineage, and friend.
rows.anchor: وكانت العرب يتخذون الأخلاء في الجاهلية، فأنزل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Say: He is God, One” answers Amir's question about God's name and number.
rows.anchor: يا محمد { هو الله أحد } لقوله ما اسمه؟ وكم هو؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God, the Self-Sufficient Master” answers what God eats: He neither eats nor drinks.
rows.anchor: الله الصمد } لقوله ما طعامه؟ { الله الصمد } الذي لا يأكل ولا يشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He did not beget” means God did not take a child; He has no child by which He would be named or known.
rows.anchor: { لم يلد } يقول: ولم يتخذ ولدا { ولم يولد } [آية:3] يقول: ليس له ولد يكتنى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “None is comparable to Him” answers the question about His intimate friend: He has no equal or likeness, so He takes no friend.
rows.anchor: { ولم يكن له كفوا أحد } [آية:4] لقوله: من خليله؟ ويقول: ليس له نظير، ولا شبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After an angel crushed al-Arbad's abdomen, al-Arbad left Medina on a cloudy day and was killed by a lightning strike.
rows.anchor: فخرج يومئذ من المدينة، وكان يوما متغيما، فأدركته صاعقة في الطريق فقتلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel struck Amir's neck, producing a boil or plague; ill and denied refuge except by a leprous woman of Banu Sulul, Amir lamented dying in her house and challenged death.
rows.anchor: فوجاه جبريل، عليه السلام، في عنقه، فخرج من عنقه دبيله، ويقال: طاعون فمرض بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil connects Amir's death to the revelation that people dispute God's power although He is severe in might.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله عزو جل: وهم يجادلون في الله وهو شديد المحال [الرعد:13]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second occasion was when Meccan polytheists asked for a description of God, Amir asked whether He was made of gold, silver, iron, or copper, and Jews said Uzayr was God's son.
rows.anchor: أن مشركي مكة، قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: انعت لنا ربك وصفه لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-samad means God has no cavity like created beings; it also means the Master to whom creatures turn humbly with their needs.
rows.anchor: { الله الصمد } يعني الذي لا جوف له، كجوف المخلوقين، ويقال: الصمد السيد الذي تصمد إليه الخلائق بحوائجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not beget and is not begotten: He has no heir and no partner sharing His origin.
rows.anchor: لم يلد } فيورث، { ولم يولد } فيشارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah refutes the claims that angels are God's daughters, Uzayr is God's son, and Christ is God's son.
rows.anchor: قالوا: الملائكة بنات الرحمن، وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله، وقالت النصارى: المسيح ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God declares those claims false and has no equal or counterpart among the gods.
rows.anchor: فأكذبهم الله عز وجل، فبرأ نفسه من قولهم، فقال: { لم يلد } يعني لم يكن له ولد { ولم يولد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labid ibn Asim, also said to be Ibn A'sam, a Jewish man, bewitched the Prophet with eleven knots on a cord, hidden in a date-palm sheath in a well with seven barriers.
rows.anchor: أن لبيد بن عاصم بن مالك، ويقال: ابن أعصم اليهودي، سحر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في إحدى عشرة عقدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spell took effect for three nights and made the Prophet gravely ill, distressing the women; the protective surahs were then revealed.
rows.anchor: فدب فيه السحر، واشتد عليه ثلاث ليال، حتى مرض مرضا شديدا، وجزعت النساء، فنزلت المعوذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While the Prophet slept, he saw two angels, one at his head and one at his feet, discuss his illness as sorcery by Labid and locate it in a well and date-palm sheath.
rows.anchor: فبينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نائم إذ رأى كأن ملكين قد أتياه، فقعد أحدهما عند رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cure was to drain the well, remove and burn the date-palm sheath, and untie each knot with a verse from the two protecting surahs.
rows.anchor: تنزف البئر، ثم يخرج قشر الطلعة فيحرقه، ثم يحل العقد، كل عقدة بأية من المعوذتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet sent Ali to retrieve and burn the spell; alternatively, Gabriel told him where it was and instructed him to undo each knot while reciting a verse, after which the Prophet recovered.
rows.anchor: فاستخرج السحر وجاء به فأحرق ذلك القشر، ويقال: إن جبريل أخبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكان السحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-falaq means creation.
rows.anchor: قل أعوذ برب الفلق } يعني برب الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil of what God created refers to jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: من شر ما خلق } [آية: 2] من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghasiq means the dark night; waqaba means when its darkness enters daylight at sunset and the darkness mingles.
rows.anchor: ومن شر غاسق } يعني ظلمة الليل { إذا وقب } [آية: 3] يعني إذا دخلت ظلمة الليل في ضوء النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “blowers on knots” are sorcery and its implements: blowing spells into knots; the passage calls this incantation sinful and refers to sorceresses who incite and seize.
rows.anchor: يعني السحر وآلاته، يعني الرقية التي هي لله معصية، يعني به ما تنفثن من الرقي في العقدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envious person means the Jews who envied the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ومن شر حاسد إذا حسد } [آية: 5] يعني اليهود حين حسدوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
rows.claim: Gabriel identified the two protecting surahs, al-Falaq and al-Nas, as the best refuge people can seek.
rows.anchor: ألا أخبرك بأفضل ما تعوذ به المتعوذون؟ قال: يا جبريل، ما هو؟ قال: المعوذتان

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said he had been told and had told the people, and instructed them to say what he said.
rows.anchor: قيل لي، فقلت لكم، فقولوا كما أقول

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud did not recite the two protecting surahs in the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: قال: وكان ابن مسعود لا يقرأ بهما في المكتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded the Prophet to seek refuge in the Lord, King, and God of all people—righteous and corrupt, wicked and good.
rows.anchor: أن يتعوذ برب الناس هو { ملك الناس } [آية: 2] بملكهم فى برهم ومجرمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whispering retreating one is Satan, depicted as a pig-shaped being attached to the heart in a human body and moving through it like blood; God gave him authority over that person.
rows.anchor: وهو الشيطان في صورة خنزير معلق بالقلب في جسد ابن آدم، وهو يجري مجرى الدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan whispers in people's hearts; when a person remembers God, Satan withdraws from the heart and leaves the body, which explains “the retreating one.”
rows.anchor: والخناس الذي إذا ذكر الله ابن آدم خنس عن قلبه، فذهب عنه، ويخرج عن جسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final verse commands seeking refuge from the evil of jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: ثم أمره الله أن يتعوذ { من } شر { الجنة والناس } [آية: 6] يعني الجن والإنس
